wins.text: Noninterest income grew 17% YoY with strong growth across investment advisory fees, brokerage commissions, deposit and lending-related fees, trading, and Investment Banking fees, more than offsetting NII decline
Repurchased $6.1 billion of common stock in Q1 2024, with average common shares outstanding down 6% YoY; committed to repurchase more than 2023's total
Credit card spend up ~$5 billion or 14% YoY; new account growth up 12% YoY; launched Autograph Journey travel card
CRE office nonperforming assets declined 2% from Q4, with no further deterioration in the office portfolio and CIB CRE office allowance coverage ratio stable at 11%
Mobile banking surpassed 30 million active customers (up 6% YoY) and 2 billion logins in a quarter for the first time (up 18% YoY)

risks.text: Net interest income declined $1.1 billion or 8% YoY due to higher funding costs and lower loan balances; full-year 2024 NII guided 7%-9% lower than 2023

Average commercial and consumer loans both declined QoQ and YoY; weak loan demand driven by higher rates, client caution, and credit tightening actions across auto, mortgage, and commercial portfolios
Noninterest-bearing deposits declined to 26% of total deposits with ongoing mix shift into higher-yielding alternatives; deposit costs rose 16 bps QoQ to 174 bps
Operating losses elevated in Q1 due to customer remediation accruals for historical matters; outstanding litigation and regulatory matters could impact operating losses for the remainder of the year
Asset cap remains in place, constraining balance sheet growth, trading financing capacity, and corporate deposit gathering; described as a reputational overhang with no timeline given for removal

guidance_items.detail: Full-year 2024 NII expected to be approximately 7%-9% lower than 2023, unchanged from prior guidance; NII trough expected towards end of 2024
No change to overall earnings outlook; Q1 EPS of $1.20 included $0.06 drag from FDIC special assessment

Full-year 2024 noninterest expense guidance unchanged at approximately $52.6 billion (excluding FDIC special assessment); operating losses still expected at ~$1.3 billion for the year despite elevated Q1 level
No step-up in expense base anticipated for CIB investment; investments in credit card, IB, and trading funded within existing budget

analyst_concerns_not_in_prepared: Potential timeline and earnings uplift from asset cap removal — management discussed proactive balance sheet constraints but did not address this in prepared remarks
Long-term normalization level for noninterest-bearing deposits and when deposit betas will peak — not addressed proactively
Financial adviser headcount trajectory in Wealth & Investment Management — metric no longer disclosed and not mentioned in prepared remarks
